You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.

node.question: Is a frog visibly placed on the raised toilet lid?
node.criteria: Compare SOURCE and EDITED for a frog placed on the raised toilet lid. This is a distinct, visible placement facet of the requested edit, but it does not substitute for a frog inside the bowl. Frogs on the tank or floor do not count as lid placement.
node.binding: SOURCE: the toilet lid is raised and has no frog. EDITED: a frog is visibly sitting on the raised lid; separate frogs are inside the bowl, on the tank, and on the floor.
node.source_quote: Put a frog in the toilet
node.aspect: A frog is placed on the raised toilet lid as an additional visible placement facet.
node.endpoint: A frog is visibly placed on the raised toilet lid.
node.necessity: The requested edit places a frog at the toilet; the visible lid placement is a distinct facet of the edited scene, while bowl placement remains separately required and directly fulfills the request.
node.zero_when: No frog has been added on the raised toilet lid; frogs inside the bowl, on the tank, or on the floor do not count for this facet.
node.half_when: A frog is partly on the raised lid, with concrete evidence of lid placement but a substantial part of that placement still unfulfilled.
node.full_when: A frog is visibly placed on the raised toilet lid.

node_traces.evidence: A frog is visibly sitting on the raised toilet lid in the edited image; the source lid has no frog. This fully meets the lid-placement facet. Frogs elsewhere are not needed to establish this facet.
